nodes.summary: This section fixes the constants of the multiplication certificate and translates each of its templates into a mathematical predicate. All statements here are exact equivalences for the constructed templates, proved from the semantics of the expression language; the arithmetic happens in the soundness and completeness sections.
nodes.title: The certificate and its semantics

nodes.summary: Completeness says that the multiplication template accepts $(\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(ab))$ for all integers $a,b$. It uses the slope representation, a consequence of the twenty-two-prime pattern 22P, to choose the slopes, pole completeness PC to supply the pole witnesses, and the generator certificate (hence Mordell-Weil) through the fixed-scalar and guard semantics. It does not use the six-contact estimate.

nodes.title: Correctness of the multiplication template

nodes.summary: Let $S_0=\{2,3,5,7,13\}$ and let $\Phi(B)$ be the rational solubility of the pole polynomial $Q_{\rm pole}$ with input $B$, as in pole completeness (that article is linked for the definition of $\Phi$ only; the hypothesis PC is not assumed). If $B\in\mathbb Q$, $B\ne0$ and $\Phi(B)$, then for every prime $p\notin S_0$ it is not the case that $v_p(B)$ is negative and odd.
nodes.title: The one-sided pole obstruction

nodes.summary: Soundness says that every rational triple accepted by the multiplication template consists of codes $\iota(n_1),\iota(n_2),\iota(n_3)$ with $n_3=n_1n_2$. It uses the generator certificate (hence Mordell-Weil) to give the inputs indices, the pole obstruction at single primes, and the six-contact height estimate H. It does not use pole completeness or the prime pattern.
